title: Peter Gunn Theme: Beginner Riff, Finger Exercise & Picking Technique
summary: JustinGuitar presents the Peter Gunn theme as a beginner-friendly riff that doubles as a finger and picking exercise. The lesson demonstrates a specific four-finger fretting pattern (1st finger on the 2nd fret, 2nd on the 3rd, 3rd on the 4th, and the little finger on the 5th) played on the thicker string with the open-string notes forming the pattern Open, Open, 2, Open, 3, Open, 5, 4. He emphasizes hand position, finger spread, and consistent pick-hand motion (downstrokes) while practicing even eighth-note rhythms (counting 1 and 2 and 3 and 4). The video also covers muting to prevent unwanted string ringing, discusses common beginner pitfalls, and frames the riff as both a musical exercise and a confidence-building practice routine. A left-handed version is referenced (Nitsuj Series), and Justin notes the pace is faster than most beginners can comfortably play, encouraging steady practice and perseverance. The overall aim is to develop finger independence, timing, and picking accuracy beyond simply memorizing the riff.
